doc.title: Bobby Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Best experience now, and past stints with Spanier, Condon and Hackett
summary: Gordon is happiest playing with Grosz, Robinson, Ingham and Smith and The Orphan Newsboys, after short earlier stints with Spanier, Condon, Hackett and McPartland.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Well what I’m doing now is what I really enjoy. I’ve never enjoyed anything so much because I’m getting a chance to play with musicians that are great New York musicians, and as I say again, a lot of them are here today: Scott Robinson, Marty Grosz, Keith Ingham, Hal Smith. Just in the last ten or fifteen years I’ve been getting into that type of music and being lucky enough to make a lot of recordings with Marty and do a lot of appearances. I’ve been to Japan twice. I’d say this is the most musical feeling I’ve had, the best musical experience I’ve had for a long time. But years ago I used to play with

Muggsy Spanier and I played with Eddie Condon and Bobby Hackett and Jimmy McPartland. That was just little stints, eight weeks here, maybe sixteen weeks there, three weeks there. But now that I’m doing a lot of recordings with Marty and we have a little group called The Orphan Newsboys, I’m really at my happiest experiences right now.
